accuracy.evidence: Mechanism conventions match the AQA 7405 (3.3.4.2), OCR A H432 (4.1.3) and Edexcel 9CH0 specifications: full-headed arrows move electron pairs, tails start on bonds or lone pairs, H–Br breaks heterolytically with Br⁻ leaving, the π bond attacks δ+ H, Br₂ is polarised by an induced dipole, and propene gives 2-bromopropane via the secondary carbocation (tertiary > secondary > primary by positive inductive effect).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips examiners report: tails on atoms or on positive charges (WHY.atom and 'plus' feedback), arrows drawn backwards from H to the C=C, arrows from Br to the π bond, confusing full and fish-hook arrows (prediction plus 'one' feedback), picking the primary carbocation for propene, and assuming non-polar Br₂ cannot be an electrophile.

lab_distinct.evidence: A drag-to-draw curly-arrow canvas: learners drag from bond and lone-pair sources to atoms, each wrong pairing gets its own reason, the scene redraws to the intermediate (carbocation plus Br⁻) once both step-one arrows are right, then a tap-the-carbon propene step and a Br₂ induced-dipole scene. No other lab draws mechanisms; it passed the 30% shingle gate against all registered labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: Sequence builds the skill: one arrow for heterolytic fission of H–Br, then the two coupled arrows of step one with ethene, then the bromide lone pair closing the carbocation, then choosing which carbon the H joins in propene by carbocation stability, then the learner applies the same arrows unaided to bromine where the dipole is induced rather than permanent.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then settles: whether the tail goes on the atom that moves (it goes on the pair), which end of HBr the π pair heads for (the δ+ H, not δ− Br), which propene product is major (2-bromopropane, not 1-bromopropane), and whether non-polar Br₂ can react (yes, the π bond induces a dipole).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with twelve distinct m= messages that name the exact slip, e.g. 'A positive atom has no spare pair to give. The tail goes on the electrons.' and '1-bromopropane forms through the less stable primary carbocation, so it is the minor product.' A streak counter rewards consecutive correct answers.

readability.evidence: Learner kid text reads within the ≤6.5 FK target using short sentences while keeping exact A-level terms (π bond, δ+, carbocation, bromide ion, heterolytic fission in adult text); adult text was rewritten into short sentences to meet the ≤9.5 target and the validator passed for all 254 lessons.

no_filler.evidence: Every step makes the learner draw or choose something that is then checked: no decorative animation, each WHY message explains a specific wrong arrow, and the lesson's sorter, practice and mastery items each test electron-pair donors and acceptors, arrow counting, mole ratios or Markovnikov selection.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 dark and 360×640 Android light show all molecules, labels and buttons on screen with no overflow; atoms and bond sources have 26px or 7%-of-width hit radii, and the 'From:' buttons plus tap-the-atom fallback let learners draw arrows without precise dragging.

accessibility.evidence: Every arrow source has a 'From:' button and atoms accept taps, so the whole lab works without dragging; the canvas aria-label lists remaining electron pairs and atoms, feedback is in an aria-live status region, and walk.cjs ran axe on desktop and iPhone 13 in both themes with no violations reported by the browser gate.
